follow-up time: From birth to early adolescence (median = 13 years)
outcome: HOMA-IR (homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance)
cohort: 942 mother-child pairs enrolled during pregnancy in obstetric practices
finding: Adolescents born by cesarean section had significantly lower adiponectin levels and suggestive evidence of higher insulin resistance compared to those born vaginally.
mod_finding: Adolescents born by cesarean section show small differences in adiponectin and insulin relative to adolescents born vaginally.
followup_time: Mid-childhood (median = 7 years) and early adolescence (median = 13 years)
